name: Hidden Hollow RV Park
note: Small family-run RV park on a private drive in a wooded hollow below the Moundsville Country Club, five minutes from downtown Moundsville in the northern panhandle; owned and operated by Derek and his father Jerry. Operator's own site: 15 spacious full-hookup sites of over 2,030 sq ft with grassed yards, 20/30/50-amp electric, 4-inch sewer risers and county water at a high +/- 120 psi (a regulator is required), basic complimentary wifi with a Comcast option, weekly garbage service, pet-friendly with breed restrictions, and golf course access next door. Open year round and genuinely transient as well as long-stay: the rate sheet (published 02/03/2026) carries daily and weekly payment links alongside monthly ones, and stays under 30 nights are taxed at the 6% WV sales tax rate 'as like a hotel room would be taxed', with month-to-month arrangements tax-exempt. Full hookups start at $30/night. No maximum RV length is stated and the sites are oversized, so a 23-ft rig is no constraint. Reserve by phone or through the site's payment links; card payments carry a convenience fee. RV Life 5*/$$ ~$30/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
inclusion_evidence: Operator's own home and Registration & Rates pages at hiddenhollowrv.com (fetched 2026-09-15, rate sheet dated 02/03/2026): 15 full-hookup sites with 20/30/50-amp service, daily and weekly payment links, and stays under 30 days taxed 'as like a hotel room' -> a real transient drive-in RV campground rather than a monthly-only or workforce park. Esri imagery at the pinned loop shows roughly 12-16 RVs on spaced individual grass/gravel pads around a private drive below the golf course, with the owners' house and pool at the south end - not packed storage or inventory.

lead.water_body: Ohio River (distant); operator says the property borders the Ohio River Islands National Wildlife Refuge at Captina Island
lead.note: The sites sit inland in a wooded hollow with the golf course between them and the river - on Esri imagery the Ohio is roughly 700 m west beyond the fairways and a rail line, with no water visible at pad level. Treat the refuge-boundary claim as a property-line fact, not a shoreline one.
